newsitem.title: USA: Miami Airport to remain LatAm cargo hub - Amerijet.
newsitem.headline: Miami Airport to remain LatAm cargo hub - Amerijet.

text.p: Miami International Airport will not be unseated any time soon as the top airport for Latin American cargo, Amerijet International Inc President David Bassett told Reuters in an interview this week.
"Miami is the capital of Latin America," Bassett said.

"There are many nay-sayers about Miami," he said, "but the reality is, there are 500 freight forwarders with Latin American experience in and around Miami International. What other city can match that?"

In fact, all-cargo Amerijet has its corporate headquarters in Fort Lauderdale, an hour north of Miami, but Bassett said he cannot fly his planes out of Fort Lauderdale's airport because it lacks the infrastructure of Miami International.
"There is nobody in Fort Lauderdale," he said.
Miami and its airport are often criticized as a difficult place to do business due to problems including a high rate of cargo theft, congested roadways and language problems.
Miami International handled 1.6 million tons of cargo in 1995, up 19 percent from 1994.

In contrast Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport handled 166,877 tons, an 11 percent increase. Atlanta's Hartsfield International Airport, often mentioned as a potential Miami International competitor, handled 771,389 tons of cargo, according to Airports Council International.
Privately-held Amerijet flies at least 20 scheduled weekly flights to the Caribbean and Latin America using its 12 Boeing 727 freighters.
Amerijet recently began service to Venezuela and plans to begin service soon to the Dominican Republic, Pamela Rollins, vice president said.

Amerijet carried the 10th most internationl freight through Miami International in 1995, handling 40,443 tons of interantional cargo. That is about 2.9 percent of the airport's total and double the amount the carrier handled in 1994.
